notes.type_correctness: GameMode = 'classic' | 'monochrome' exported from types.ts (root of type tree). All consumers use it via type imports. createGameState(mode: GameMode = 'classic') signature is sound.
notes.pattern_adherence: resolveCellColor() and resolveActiveColor()/resolveGhostColor() helpers follow the same pattern as CELL_COLORS lookup — small pure helpers above the class, consistent with existing boardRenderer.ts style. flushMode() mirrors flushActions() drain pattern.
notes.test_coverage: 4 engine tests cover gameMode default, monochrome argument, propagation through ticks, and pause/resume cycle. 6 mainMenu tests cover button count, flushMode null before interaction, MONOCHROME enqueues Start and 'monochrome', PLAY leaves mode null, drain after flush. Missing: renderer-layer color value tests (no unit test asserting 0xeeeeee/0x888888/0x555555 at render call sites) — not blocking since renderer tests are integration-level by convention in this codebase.
notes.security: Pure UI/rendering change. No network I/O, no storage writes, no user data handling. GameState.gameMode is not persisted per spec (confirmed: createGameState() with no arg defaults to 'classic' on restart/navigate-to-title).
notes.architectural_alignment: GameMode in engine/types.ts (correct — shared root). gameMode field in GameState is opaque to engine logic (engine never branches on it). Renderer and UI consume it at draw time. pendingMode handling in main.ts correctly resets to 'classic' after use. No layer boundary violations.
